summary.headline: Axis Max Life H1 FY27 VNB up 21% to INR1,180 crore with margin at 25.4%; Q2 individual APE growth slowed to 9%.
summary.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 VNB of INR1,180 crore (up 21%) with VNB margin expanding 210 bps to 25.4%, and Q2 VNB margin of about 27% despite GST. Individual adjusted APE grew 12% in H1 but only 9% in Q2, with Axis Bank APE up 4% in Q2 and annuities up 130%. Management is confident of H2 APE acceleration and of margins closer to 26% for FY27, while stating the EoM consultation paper's commission and EoM caps are manageable. Capital is at 197% solvency with no immediate capital raise planned.

financial_highlights.change: up 17% YoY; renewal INR11,247 crore up 18%
improved 174 bps YoY; 11.7% ex-GST vs 14.6% in H1 FY26
INR686 crore debt raised in September

segments.name: Proprietary channels
segments.commentary: Total APE up 9% in Q2 on a high base (3-year CAGR 25%); e-commerce up 29% in Q2.

segments.name: Partnership channels
segments.commentary: APE up 11% in H1 and 8% in Q2; Axis Bank APE up 4% in Q2 (8% in H1); retail partnerships up 19% in Q2; group credit life up 41% in Q2.

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: H1 growth about 4%, with August-September growth near 8%; annuity up around 50% and protection up 27% in agency.

segments.name: Retail product mix (Q2)
segments.commentary: ULIP 37%, annuity 19%, participating and non-participating savings 15% each, protection and health 14%; Smart RISE contributes around 8% of APE; annuity up 130% in Q2.

guidance_outlook: VNB margin guidance range of 25% to 26% retained, with management now seeing FY27 closer to 26% (about 25.5% mentioned as a floor-type view).
APE growth expected to accelerate in H2 FY27 versus H1, with a favourable base in protection notwithstanding a high protection base.

Under the EoM consultation paper, management expects EoM to fall from about 22% to 16.5%-17.5% with commission changes, then to 15% and eventually 12.5%, via about 5-7% from commission and GST adjustments and 2-3% from efficiency measures.
Core opex growth expected in the high single digits (8%-10%); total EoM ratio for FY27 expected to remain around 25%, similar to last year.
No immediate capital raise planned given 197% solvency; Ind AS transition date 1 April 2026, with FY27 comparatives to be restated when FY28 is reported.
capex_capacity: Solvency ratio at 197%; INR686 crore of debt raised in September 2026.
Annuity refresh planned for Q4 FY27; protection product refresh underway, including relaunch of Smart Term Plan Plus with 8 variants and life cover up to age 100.
GIFT City NRI proposition scaling; GIFT City contributing more than 5% of ULIP APE.
More than 47 AI solution tracks; AI-enabled models delivered nearly INR1,000 crore of risk avoidance; financial frictionless underwriting supports half of protection business.
demand_pricing: Axis Bank Q2 APE up 4% with counter share around 62%-63% in Q2 (versus about 65% normally), attributed to product-led calls, a delayed STPP launch and ULIP softness; management expects recovery by year-end.

Axis Bank contributes about 42%-43% of sales; agency about 21%; D2C 6%-7%; direct sales force about 12%; Yes Bank 5%-6%; small banks about 3%; brokers 2%-3%; GCL impact limited to about 1% of business.
Protection: post-GST surge saw 80%-85% incremental customers; management assumes moderation in protection growth on a high base. Pure retail protection grew 31% in Q2.
Non-par is declining; management attributes part of this to annuity cannibalisation, with a high non-par base and a persistency issue in discontinued non-par designs (discontinued in March 2026).
Management said the 13-month persistency is 83% versus 85% last year, while long-term persistency at the 37th, 49th and 61st months reached record highs.

qa_highlights.question: What APE growth and VNB margin are feasible in H2 given the high protection base and declining non-par?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects APE growth to accelerate in H2 versus H1, and sees margins as improving through volume-led operating leverage, with 25%-26% guidance retained and FY27 closer to 26%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EoM reduction comes from commission cuts, and how will 12.5% be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: Commission cuts take EoM to about 16.5%-17.5%; further gains come from commission and GST adjustments (5%-7%) and efficiency (2%-3%); management is confident of reaching 15% and 12.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Axis Bank losing counter share, and how will consolidation play out?
qa_highlights.answer: Counter share was about 62%-63% in Q2 versus about 65% normally; management expects it to return to around 65% by year-end and says no formal consolidation talks have occurred.

qa_highlights.question: Why was new business strain up about 20% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to credit life business and the GST charge introduced in H1 FY27, which was absent in the prior year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the variable annuity driving margin gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Variable annuity contributed more than 50% of Q2 annuity sales but margins are similar to existing products, so it did not drive the margin lift.

qa_highlights.question: Are capital raise plans needed?
qa_highlights.answer: No immediate capital requirement; solvency is 197%, and EoM and IFRS/RBC changes reduce strain on capital.

risks_watch: EoM consultation paper: final draft terms, GST treatment in EoM, and the transition period remain open.
Axis Bank counter share and growth recovery in H2; Axis Bank APE growth of 4% in Q2.
Protection growth normalisation on a high base after the GST-led surge.
Persistency: 13-month persistency at 83% versus 85%; management expects improvement from Q3.
Ind AS transition and IGAAP parallel reporting for two years; EoM computation post-transition unclear.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins, H2 growth and the EoM path, while cautious and somewhat defensive on Axis Bank growth, protection moderation and persistency. Management repeatedly called the EoM framework a consultation paper still under discussion.
key_quotes: So we are more confident that APE growth should look better in the second half than the first half.
I think as the year is progressing, possibly now confidence is more towards closer towards 26% than anything else.
So we do not see any kind of a downside as far as this 42 -43% of our sales is concerned.
Persistency stress is actually concentrated in the Non-Par design as we had told in the last call as well.

growth.why: Management holds VNB margin guidance of 25-26% (closer to 26% for FY27) and expects H2 APE growth to beat H1's 11-12%, backed by Axis Bank counter recovery, protection refresh and annuity launch, though Q2 APE slowed to 8-9% and no capacity additions or quantified orders were given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: VNB margin up 210 bps to 25.4% in H1 and about 27% in Q2, with management holding 25%-26% guidance and seeing FY27 closer to 26%, driven by volume-led operating leverage and a policyholder opex ratio that improved 174 bps to 13.7% of GWP.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants, branches or capacity additions were discussed; the call covered product refreshes (annuity in Q4 FY27, Smart Term Plan Plus relaunch) rather than physical capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects H2 APE growth to beat H1's 11-12%, backed by Axis Bank counter share recovering from about 62%-63% to around 65% by year-end, though Q2 individual APE growth slowed to 9% and Axis Bank APE rose only 4%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Solvency is at 197% with no immediate capital raise planned and INR686 crore of debt raised in September 2026, so no new capital program is signalled; utilisation is not a relevant metric for an insurer.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: VNB margin guidance of 25%-26% was held rather than raised, with FY27 only seen 'closer to 26%'; no upgrade to APE or VNB growth guidance was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Risks include the EoM consultation paper's open terms, Axis Bank counter share at 62%-63% versus about 65% normally, protection normalising on a high post-GST base, and 13-month persistency at 83% versus 85%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Annuity refresh is planned for Q4 FY27, and the Smart Term Plan Plus relaunch (8 variants, cover up to age 100) is underway; Smart RISE already contributes about 8% of APE and annuity sales rose 130% in Q2.

rows.label: EoM ratio reduction via commission cuts
rows.why: Management expects EoM to fall from about 22% to 16.5%-17.5% from commission changes, then toward 15% and 12.5% via 5-7% commission/GST adjustments and 2-3% efficiency gains, though the consultation paper's final terms remain open; FY27 total EoM is guided to stay around 25%.

rows.label: Core opex growth held to high single digits
rows.why: Core opex growth guided at 8%-10% against APE growth of about 9-12%, supporting operating leverage.

rows.label: Axis Bank counter share recovery
rows.why: Counter share fell to about 62%-63% in Q2 from a normal 65% on product-led calls, a delayed STPP launch and ULIP softness; recovery depends on the STPP launch and ULIP demand.

tone.note: Management was confident on VNB margins (25%-26%, FY27 closer to 26%), H2 APE acceleration and the EoM path, but defensive on Axis Bank counter share, protection moderation after the GST-led surge and persistency; analysts pushed on the Q2 slowdown and how the EoM reduction to 12.5% would be reached
